description: Cut an image down to an aspect ratio or an exact region, and/or turn it by quarter turns or mirror it, on-device (same tool as ruah.tools/crop: whole pixels moved, never resampled). aspect_ratio keeps the largest centred area of that shape (e.g. "1:1" for a square profile picture, "16:9" for a video thumbnail, "4:5" for a portrait post). box keeps an exact region, in pixels of the input as it is shown (upright). rotate and the flips work alone or together with either. Saves a new file and reports which region of the input it kept; the original is never changed. To change the pixel size use `resize`; to change only the format or file size use `compress`.

aspect_ratio.description: Width:height of the result, e.g. "1:1", "4:5", "3:2", "16:9". Keeps the largest centred area of that shape (after rotate). Give this or box, not both.

box.description: Exact region to keep, in pixels of the input as shown (upright), measured before rotate and flips. Give this or aspect_ratio, not both.

format.description: Output format: keep = same as the input; webp = usually smallest, keeps transparency; avif = smaller still, slower; jpeg = photos only, transparency becomes white; png = keeps transparency. Default keep.

input_path.description: Image file to crop. Absolute, ~/…, or relative to the working directory.

lossless.description: png only: keep exact colours. Default true; false makes a smaller palette PNG.

output_path.description: Where to save. Default: "<name>-crop.<ext>" next to the input. Existing files are never overwritten.

quality.description: 1–100 for webp/avif/jpeg. Default 90, like the web crop tool.

rotate.description: Turn clockwise by this many degrees: 90, 180 or 270 (-90 turns anticlockwise). Default 0.

name: crop
title: Crop, rotate or flip image
